clue.text: Book? Bad, or (put another way) written in hurry, lacking detail

indicators.note: putting something another way rearranges it, so the letters of these two words are reordered

parts.note: a rush is a hurry

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a hastily written, badly done book that skimps on detail.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and brackets make the surface read as a review; 'put another way' rearranges BAD OR into ROADB, and 'written in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-brush approach is a general, sweeping one that ignores fine particulars.

clue.text: Academic degree, beyond a young child

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
by can mean past or beyond, as in 'go by the house'

explanation.surface: A degree is earned once someone has grown beyond being a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is an infant, the youngest kind of child.

clue.text: Plant not badly placed on crag with eroded edges

parts.note: OK means all right, so not badly

indicators.note: the crag has its outer letters worn away, leaving only its middle

explanation.surface: A plant that is doing fine has found a spot on a weathered crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed on' sets OK above RA in this down clue; RA is what remains of CRAG once 'with eroded edges' removes its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a vegetable plant grown for its edible green pods, also called lady's fingers.

clue.text: Lord upset about cold ruler's excessively outmoded punishment device

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed word surrounds the other pieces
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lud is the form of 'lord' used in addressing a judge, as in 'm'lud'
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a king is a ruler; the possessive gives the S
too means excessively, as in 'too hot'

explanation.surface: A peer, annoyed about a cold monarch, objects to an old-fashioned punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LUD to DUL, and 'about' wraps that round the rest. 'Lud' is how barristers address a judge ('m'lud').
explanation.definitionFit: A ducking stool was a chair on a beam used to plunge offenders, often scolds, into water, a punishment long abandoned.

clue.text: Chaucerian pilgrim on vigil?

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a memo heading
an eve is the evening before a feast, traditionally kept as a vigil

explanation.surface: Asks whether one of Chaucer's pilgrims was keeping watch overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reeve is one of the storytellers in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reeve, an estate manager, is a pilgrim who tells a tale in the Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Group going into shelter severe

annotationWithheld.why: 'Group going into shelter severe': RING inside STENT gives the letters, but a stent is a medical tube, not a shelter, and TENT plus RING leaves the opening S with no source; a word seems lost in OCR

clue.text: King in power with very big advantages

indicators.note: in places the king's letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
OS stands for outsize, very big
R is short for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch holding power and great size enjoys many advantages.
explanation.definitionFit: Pros are points in favour, as in 'pros and cons'.

clue.text: Hard to catch a programme providing music

indicators.note: to catch means to hold, so the first word encloses the others

parts.note: rocky means hard or difficult, as in a rocky patch
a bill is a programme of entertainment, as on a playbill

explanation.surface: It's hard to catch a show that offers music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' is ROCKY (as in a rocky time), not the usual H; 'to catch' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockabilly is an early form of rock and roll blending rhythm and blues with hillbilly country.

clue.text: Drips get in all over the place, becoming cause of high water level

indicators.note: scattered all over the place, the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Water drips in everywhere and the level rises.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring tide is the especially high tide near new and full moon.

clue.text: Tree, one right alongside trench after it's been chopped, covered with fruit

indicators.note: the pieces are covered, so they go inside the fruit word

parts.note: a berry is a fruit
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the letters of 'it' are chopped out of the trench word

parts.note: a ditch is a trench

explanation.surface: A tree beside a trench, once hacked back, ends up laden with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after it's been chopped' cuts IT from the trench word, leaving DCH; 'covered with' wraps the fruit around the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird cherry is a European tree whose small black fruit is eaten by birds.

clue.text: Award, not first, having lasting effect

indicators.note: not first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: an Oscar is a film award

explanation.surface: Losing out on the top award leaves its mark on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not first' removes the O from OSCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left behind long after the injury, physical or emotional.

clue.text: If one gets work as nightwatchman it won't be as originally planned

definitions.text: If one gets work as nightwatchman it won't be as originally planned

parts.words: If one gets work as nightwatchman it won't be as originally planned
parts.note: in cricket a nightwatchman is a lower-order batter sent in late in a day's play to protect a better one, so the planned sequence of batters changes

explanation.surface: Taking a night job as a guard upsets someone's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a security guard; in cricket the nightwatchman is a tail-end batter promoted to bat out the last overs of a day, which changes who goes in when.
explanation.definitionFit: The list setting out who bats in which position is altered when a nightwatchman is sent in early.

clue.text: Frequently excellent, in opening round, followed with appreciation

annotationWithheld.why: 'Frequently excellent, in opening round, followed with appreciation': GAIN is appreciation, but no reading of 'excellent, in opening round' gives TIMEANDA; a word may be misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Frequently excellent, in opening round, followed with appreciation

clue.text: Spiteful volume- 14 on a roll?

annotationWithheld.why: 'Spiteful volume- 14 on a roll?': V is volume, but '14 on a roll' gives no INDICTIVE; the clue looks garbled in OCR and the cross-reference cannot be resolved

clue.text: Set to pick winners, being on a roll?

definitions.text: Set to pick winners, being on a roll?

parts.words: Set to pick winners, being on a roll?
parts.note: the set is a body of people who choose successful candidates, and 'on a roll' refers to the electoral register, not a winning streak

explanation.surface: A team on a winning streak seems ready to choose the winners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a roll' suggests a run of success; here it means being listed on the electoral roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters as a body choose who wins an election and are listed on the register of voters.

clue.text: Bad English, dreadful bilge, impossible to read

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

indicators.note: dreadful signals that the following word is badly mangled

explanation.surface: Poor English written as dreadful rubbish cannot be read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges BILGE into GIBLE; 'Bad' supplies ILL rather than being an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegible handwriting or print cannot be deciphered.

clue.text: University in Brazil with charm, not an austere architectural style

indicators.note: in places the university letter inside the rest

parts.note: BR is the international code for Brazil

indicators.note: not removes the word that follows from the charm word

parts.note: a talisman is a lucky charm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Brazilian university, charming but plain, is built in a severe style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with charm, not an' looks like describing the university; 'not an' trims TALISMAN to TALISM, and 'in' sets U just after BR, Brazil's country code.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutalism is a 1950s-70s style of building in bare concrete, known for its stark severity.

clue.text: Clown brought about second surprise

indicators.note: brought about here means placed around, so the clown word goes round the other letter

parts.note: a twit is a fool, a clown

explanation.surface: A clown arranged a second unexpected turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' looks like 'caused', but here it puts TWIT around S.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is an unexpected development, as in a plot twist.

clue.text: Tube in which there's a coin

indicators.note: the tube contains the next letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: a duct is a tube or channel

explanation.surface: A coin has been dropped into a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat is an old gold or silver coin once used across Europe.

clue.text: Faulty nut, slanting, sorted out

indicators.note: faulty indicates the following word is broken and reassembled

parts.note: angled means slanting

explanation.surface: A faulty nut on a slanting bolt finally gets fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faulty' rearranges NUT to UNT, followed by ANGLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untangled has had its knots removed, so it is straightened out.

clue.text: Pretty crazy, on reflection, 7 in talk before start of extraordinary fight

indicators.note: in puts the reflected word inside the talk word

parts.note: chat is talk

indicators.note: reflection shows a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy

indicators.note: start of takes only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: box means fight with fists

explanation.surface: A crazy argument breaks out in conversation before an extraordinary fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns LOCO into OCOL and 'in' puts it inside the talk word. The '7' in the OCR text adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate-box describes something conventionally and sentimentally attractive, like the pictures on old sweet boxes.

clue.text: More heartless tax raised? Time's needed to comprehend it

indicators.note: to comprehend means to take in, so the time word encloses the other piece

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised turns letters upwards, so they read backwards
heartless removes the middle, keeping only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A tax lifted heartlessly needs time for people to understand it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves TX and 'raised' turns it upward in this down clue; 'it' simply points back to the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, as in 'extra helpings'.

clue.text: Historian in meeting with restrained Democrat

indicators.note: restrained means held in, so the meeting word holds the next letter

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for work or competition, as in a spelling bee

explanation.surface: A historian attends a meeting alongside a quiet Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: BEE as a social meeting is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk who wrote the Ecclesiastical History of the English People.

clue.text: Ship's steward's utterance to attract attention

indicators.note: the possessive 's reads as 'has', so these words have the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A ship's steward calls quietly to catch a passenger's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is a hissing sound made to get someone's attention discreetly.

clue.text: Goodness exists, certainly 8

parts.note: is means exists, as in 'there is'
ay is an old form of yes, meaning certainly

explanation.surface: Goodness really does exist, of that there is no doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: The '8' in the OCR text adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, like 'well, well'.

clue.text: Ability shown by soldier, determined fellow carrying 11 dispatch back

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: back means read in reverse
carrying means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: set means determined, as in 'set on going'
send means dispatch

explanation.surface: Talent is displayed by a soldier, a resolute man sending a message back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' makes SSENDET and 'back' reverses it all to TEDNESS. The '11' in the OCR text adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Giftedness is natural talent or exceptional aptitude.

clue.text: Happening to have no time for uniform

indicators.note: to have no removes the next letter from the word

parts.note: an event is a happening

explanation.surface: Something occurs with no time to change into uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have no' takes T out of EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level, regular or consistent throughout.

clue.text: Damage caused by rascal in a term, running wild

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naughty child runs wild during term and causes damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running wild' rearranges IN A TERM into AIRMENT; 'caused by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Impairment is weakening or harm to a faculty or function.
